issues.title: Adding devices to a running rack from the app has no documented recipe
issues.doing: Finding how a URL added to watch.json while the app runs gets a checker of its own, without restarting the others
issues.happened: The docs show plug/unplug in the handle table and say reload(manifest) moves a running rack to a new layout, but not how an app built on rack start does this (a device cannot reach the handle). I concluded the app needs its own main.ts that calls start() and reload(manifest), with stable slot numbers per URL and a size large enough. No guide shows that.
issues.expected: A guide section on a rack whose set of devices changes while it runs: who calls plug or reload, how slot numbers and names stay stable, how many slots there are
issues.where: Racks and Running a rack: 'Running a rack from code' shows only a static manifest; the 42U default and the size option appear only in Concepts and in a type row of the API table; the API table has one line on reload(manifest?)
issues.workaround: main.ts polls watch.json, builds a new placed manifest (size 200, checker in slot n, name checker-<slot>) and calls running.reload(manifest); unchanged checkers kept their firmware. Did not need to read source, only grepped once for the size check.

issues.title: status() is async and crashes is a number, not stated where looked
issues.doing: Reading status() in check.ts to prove a checker crashed
issues.happened: The API table lists status() without saying it returns a promise; Reports says crashes is 'the crashes within the last 60 seconds', which could be a list. A probe (scratch/probe.ts) showed a promise of an array with crashes: 0.
issues.expected: Return types spelled out (Promise<SlotStatus[]>, crashes: number)
issues.where: API, 'The rack handle'; Reports, status() table
issues.workaround: Ran a probe and printed the JSON; no source read

issues.title: Hang and crash need a cause from inside the device
issues.doing: Making check.ts cause a hang and a crash of a checker through what a test server answers
issues.happened: Nothing in the docs says how a test provokes either. A throw inside setTimeout crashes the device ('checker-7 crashed: exited with code 1'); an endless for(;;) is bitten by the event-loop watchdog after 10 s (12.4 s to recover). A checker that hangs after every reset would reach the crash limit and be faulted, so the test server hangs only once. The chaos hook behind WATCHER_CHAOS is test code in a production device.
issues.expected: A documented way to provoke a crash or a hang in a device on the bench or in a test rack
issues.where: Testing a device and Faults and overload: the bench has faults but no way to cause one
issues.workaround: An env flag read in the device, since Workers copy process.env when they start
